design.name: 神火飞鸦
design.brief: A divine fire crow (神火飞鸦), the Ming-dynasty winged rocket bomb shaped like a crow, brought to life in the fire god's forge as a flying kamikaze: a crow-shaped construct about 1.6 m in wingspan made of a light bamboo frame covered in black lacquered paper, with real crow proportions (stout body, thick strong beak, fanned tail), big painted fierce red-and-gold eyes, vermilion paper wing edges; its fat round belly is a paper-and-bamboo gunpowder drum glowing lava orange through the paper seams (weak spot: the whole belly), and under each wing hang two small bamboo rocket tubes with paper fuses that it flies with. Little bamboo-and-wire legs with four clawed toes. Twitchy, shrieking, explosive.
design.style_note: Stylization: cartoon game proportions in the same family as the desert and frost rosters (jerboa soldier, fire rat, sancai tomb beast, golden snub-nosed monkey): chunky simplified masses, oversized heads and hands or paws, toy-like readable forms with clean bevelled edges. Iron, basalt and bronze as a few big faceted plates with sparse painted wear; lava and fire painted as OPAQUE glowing cracks, seams and solid sculpted flame shapes (never transparent fire, smoke or particles); fur, hair and feathers as a few large carved clumps.
design.turnaround_lead: Symmetric flying bind pose for rigging:
design.turnaround_pose: flying in a symmetric T-pose: both wings spread fully and horizontally to the sides, straight and level; the body level, head facing straight ahead, beak closed; the tail fanned flat behind; the two rocket tubes under each wing pointing straight backwards; both little legs tucked under the belly; the belly painted opaque glowing orange through the paper seams (no flames, no sparks, no smoke trails); IMPORTANT, true orthographic geometry: in the two SIDE views each spread wing is seen exactly edge-on as a thin sliver, never as a spread fan; only the front and back views show the full wingspan
design.turnaround_digits: both wingtips, the tail and all four rocket tubes fully inside the frame (keep generous margin for the wingspan in the front and back views).
